summary: Plain code is compiled to JavaScript functions and runs 9 to 25 times faster, and a call in tail position keeps nothing of the call it is in, so a loop runs in constant memory. `["assuming", change, ..., expression]` asks what would hold after a change and leaves the database as it is. `schema/open` names the rest of a record or list, and a keyed relation can declare `"merge"`, a lattice aggregate that joins the values its key gets. When a key or an equality rule makes values one, the value kept is their least, so answers no longer depend on the order of rules or facts; this is a breaking change, as is host code that read a scope's bindings through a `Ref`. A group whose rules invent unknowns follows a change to facts one component of values at a time, and a schema whose lambda asks about itself no longer runs Lion out of memory. Research runs share one Lion model in `research/`.
